analysis.investment_thesis: KRN is a genuinely exciting niche OEM heat exchanger manufacturer riding India's cooling revolution with a real 40%+ revenue CAGR — exactly the kind of "boring product, booming demand" story I love. But at a P/E of 116x and a trailing PEG of 1.63, the market has already priced in a decade of perfection, leaving no margin of safety for a company burning ₹65 Cr of free cash flow annually.
key_strengths: Exceptional growth trajectory: Revenue CAGR 40.2% and Net Profit CAGR 71.1% over 3 years — rare execution for a ₹430 Cr revenue manufacturer.
Secular tailwind: HVAC/R components benefit from India's urbanization, data center boom, and global energy-transition cooling demand — a story visible from the street.
Nearly debt-free post-IPO: D/E of 0.06 with ₹33 Cr debt vs ₹528 Cr equity gives massive headroom to fund the next growth phase.
key_risks: PEG of 1.63 (P/E 116 ÷ earnings growth 71%) breaches my hard limit of 1.5 — even the forward PEG at ~1.46 (58.52 ÷ ~40%) offers little comfort.
Free cash flow deeply negative and worsening: FCF was -₹65 Cr in FY25 on capex of ₹151 Cr — the business is spending 7x its operating cash flow on expansion, a risky bet.
Hot IPO premium: equity base exploded from ₹130 Cr to ₹528 Cr in one year, P/S of 14.3x prices in flawless execution for years; any growth stumble will be punished severely.
red_flags: PEG ratio 1.63 — above my 1.5 red-flag threshold; market is paying for perfection.
Negative and deteriorating FCF: -₹9 Cr (FY23) → -₹41 Cr (FY24) → -₹65 Cr (FY25), capex ₹151 Cr dwarfs OCF of ₹21 Cr.
Classic hot IPO pattern: ₹258 Cr financing inflow in FY25, P/E of 116x — the crowd is already in.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KRN is the kind of small-cap niche manufacturer I built my career finding — a Neemrana-based heat exchanger supplier serving global HVAC/R OEMs with a beautifully simple story. The numbers are genuinely impressive: revenue grew from ₹156 Cr to ₹430 Cr in three years (40% CAGR), net profit from ₹11 Cr to ₹53 Cr (71% CAGR), and operating margins held steady at 16.5% even while scaling rapidly. The gross margin of 53% is unusually high for a component manufacturer and suggests real pricing power with OEM customers. Post-IPO, the balance sheet is fortress-clean at 0.06x D/E, and the ₹151 Cr capex in FY25 signals serious capacity expansion to capture export demand across Asia, Europe, and North America.

The problem is entirely in the price. At P/E of 116x, the trailing PEG is 1.63 — I don't buy above 1.5, full stop. Even using forward P/E of 58.52x and assuming 40% sustained earnings growth, the PEG is still ~1.46. Worse, free cash flow was -₹65 Cr in FY25: operating cash of just ₹21 Cr is being swamped by ₹151 Cr of capex. This is a manufacturing business, not software — those machines need to fill up with orders and convert to profit before the story justifies this multiple. I'd revisit enthusiastically below ₹600 (PEG approaching 1.0) if growth sustains, but paying 116x today for a company with negative FCF and hot-IPO sentiment baked in is a bet I'll pass on.
